name: Books Proof
office_task: Each month, rebuild a client's ledger from its source documents and check every account against its trial balance; publish the all-clear, or each difference for a person to accept with its cause.
systems_of_record: the client's ledger (Xero), read only over the Accounting API. Its trial balance at the as-of date is the master for every account balance, matched on the Xero account id. The bot rebuilds a shadow ledger from the source documents: invoices, bills, credit notes, payments, bank transactions, transfers and manual journals. Nothing is ever written to the client's ledger. Expense claims and opening (conversion) balances are not exposed over the API, so each accepted difference records its cause

the bot's own store: the shadow ledger, opened from the trial balance at a cutover date the person sets, and the history of every accepted adjustment. In production it runs on the AI Pathway connector's check_books tool (connect.aipathway.com.au) once that ships; until then the hosted step runs with us
the system the result is published into (it issues the report_id the practice opens)

emits.write: the month's books proof, written where the practice opens it: the pair contract it ran under, the join key (the Xero account id), the master (the trial balance) for every field, the as-of and cutover dates, and the counts matched, within tolerance, mismatched, orphaned and adjusted; published every month, including the all-clear
emits.readback: the report store returns a report_id, and reading that id back returns the contract id, the five counts and the published time; no id back means the run did not publish and the owner is told

emits.write: an exception naming the person who owns the client: one account whose shadow balance differs from the trial balance, with both values, the master's value and the off-by amount, waiting for that person to accept it with a cause; an account on one side only (orphan); a difference over the threshold amount; too many accounts differing; an acceptance that would write the client's ledger (refused); or an accepted adjustment whose write returned no id
emits.readback: the exception desk returns an exception_id, and reading that id back returns the account id, the reason, both values and the exception_owner; no id back means nothing was raised and the run stops
